title: Temple Holi Celebration: What to Wear to a Mandir Holi 2027
excerpt: What to wear to a temple Holi celebration abroad: modest cotton kurta sets, a dupatta for the head, shoes you can slip off and temple etiquette.
body:
For a temple Holi celebration, wear a modest cotton kurta set with pants or palazzos, covered shoulders and a dupatta you can drape over your head. Choose slip-on shoes, since you will take them off at the door, and a fabric that is comfortable for sitting on the floor through kirtan.

This guide is for women attending Holi at a mandir in the USA, UK, Canada, UAE or Australia, where the day often includes prayers, kirtan, prasad and colour play on the temple grounds. An [off-white embroidered cotton kurta set with cutwork organza dupatta](/products/off-white-embroidered-cotton-flex-kurta-pant-organza-dupatta-set/) is a graceful, respectful choice.

*By the Bahe Kurtiz styling team, Jaipur. Every piece is made in our own Jaipur unit, where our block prints are hand printed by karigars.*

## What should you wear to a temple Holi celebration?

A temple is a place of worship first and a party venue second, even on Holi. Many families bring children and elders, and the day can stretch from a morning aarti to an afternoon of colour, so comfort matters as much as looking festive. Dress as you would for any temple visit: shoulders covered, a neckline that stays modest when you bend, and a hem that covers your knees when you sit cross-legged.

A kurta set with pants or palazzos is ideal. It is modest, comfortable on the floor and easy to move in during colour play outside. Holi falls in late March 2027 (check your local calendar), and temples often hold their celebration on the nearest weekend, so check your mandir's notice board or website.

## How does a temple Holi day usually flow?

Every mandir is different, but many celebrations follow a similar pattern. Plan your outfit around each part.

| Part of the day | What usually happens | Outfit tip |
|---|---|---|
| Arrival and darshan | Shoes off, prayers inside | Slip-on shoes, dupatta ready |
| Kirtan or bhajans | Sitting on the floor for a while | Palazzos or roomy pants |
| Colour play on the grounds | Gulal outdoors, often with rules | Cotton that washes easily |
| Prasad or lunch | Sitting or standing to eat | Dupatta pinned out of the way |

## Can you play colour in your temple outfit?

Many people wear one outfit for the whole day, and that is fine as long as it is cotton and you are happy for it to get colourful. If you would rather keep your puja outfit clean, bring a second kurta set to change into for play.

Check the rules before you go. Many temples ask guests to use only the colours provided, or to bring dry, plant-based gulal, and some do not allow water. Follow what the temple asks; it keeps the grounds clean and the day pleasant for everyone.

> **From our Jaipur studio:** For a day that moves between the prayer hall and the lawn, we like lightweight cotton with a little ease at the hip, so sitting cross-legged feels natural. Embroidery near the neckline keeps the look festive for darshan, while the rest of the outfit stays simple enough to wash after play.

## What should you bring and avoid at a temple Holi?

Pack light. Most temples have a shoe rack, but it gets crowded on festival days.

- Slip-on shoes or sandals that are easy to find on a rack
- Socks if the floor is cold (helpful in UK and Canadian Marches)
- A dupatta or scarf for covering your head
- A small towel and a bag for a coloured outfit
- A donation for the temple if you wish

Arrive a little early on festival days. Parking fills up, the shoe racks get busy, and finding a good spot on the floor for kirtan is easier when you are not rushing.

Avoid short hemlines, sleeveless tops without a layer, leather items inside the temple if your mandir asks, and heavy perfume during prayers. Keep phones on silent during kirtan.

## Frequently asked questions

**What should I wear to a temple on Holi?**
A modest cotton kurta set with pants or palazzos, covered shoulders and a dupatta for your head. Slip-on shoes make the shoe rack easier.

**Do I need to cover my head at a temple Holi?**
It depends on the temple and your family. Carrying a dupatta means you are ready if it is expected.

**Can I wear jeans to a temple Holi celebration?**
Some people do, but jeans are uncomfortable for sitting on the floor and heavy once wet. A cotton kurta set is the easier choice.

**What colours can I bring to a temple Holi?**
Follow the temple's rules. Many provide colours or ask for dry, plant-based gulal only, and some do not allow water.
